Program exits with an unhandled exception. Somehow that is my fucking problem?

I had a guy that was processing 7 million records, 500k a time. His script would start by grabbing 500k records from the database and iterating over them for hours or days. If one single operation in his script timed out, he would start all over from the beginning. Then he told me it was my fault because occasionally our API endpoint would timeout. Developers have some assumption that networks handle every request instantly, memory is infinite, disks are never full. I had to guide him to have his script retry on failure, keep track of totally failed records and be able to restart where it left off.

Here is another thing I see constantly. Iterating over a large number of records. For each record make a connection to a remote API, send a single request, close conneciton. Do that over and over again until the system runs out of ephemeral ports. Somehow that's my problem. Fucking connect to the API and send as many requests as you can before it drops you! Then catch that and reconnect!

I have to explain three way handshakes, DNS, ephemeral ports, NAT, cookies, headers, load balancing over and over and over. SSL is a mystery to most of these guys. I'm not even talking about the specifics of key exchange or the principals of the encryption(I'm not so familiar with that), but just how certificate chains work.
